stories.headline: Earthquake of 6.9 magnitude hits near Ozernovskiy in Russia
stories.title: Earthquake of 6.9 magnitude hits near Ozernovskiy in Russia
stories.summary: Moscow, Oct 16: An earthquake of 6.9 magnitude struck 76 km northeast of Ozernovskiy in Russia on Friday, the US Geological Survey said. The epicentre, with a depth of 143.2 km, was initially determined to be at 52.01 degrees north latitude and 157.25 degrees east longitude, it said. A perceptible earthquake with an intensity of up to four magnitude points has been registered in Kamchatka, Russia's state-run TASS news agency reported, citing the Kamchatka branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences’ Geophysical Service. “Instrumental intensity in Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky amounted to up to four points,” scientists said. Scientists estimated its magnitude at 6.5 first, but later revised it to 6.9. It was felt as a magnitude-5 earthquake in the region, it said. “According to verified information, the magnitude of this seismic event was 6.9. Its epicentre was located on land, 156 km southwest of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, at the depth of 138 km. In Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, it was felt as a magnitude-5 earthquake,” seismologists said. A number of residents of the region’s administrative centre evacuated from their apartments because of tremors, it said. Inside residential buildings, the earthquake caused light fixtures to swing violently, doors to slam shut, and tableware to rattle. According to eyewitnesses, the tremor, which occurred at 3:36 pm local time (3:36 a.m. GMT), continued for about one minute.

stories.headline: Congress, allies seeking Bangladesh-like regime change: Rajnath
stories.title: Congress, allies seeking Bangladesh-like regime change: Rajnath
stories.summary: Lucknow, Oct 16: Union Minister Rajnath Singh on Friday lashed out at the Congress and its allies over the protests in the national capital, accusing them of seeking a regime change along the lines of Bangladesh and using the energy of youth to spread "anarchy". Addressing a press conference here, Singh asserted that democracy does not give anyone the licence to create disorder or undermine the credibility of constitutional institutions. "It appears that the Congress and its political allies, directly and through their supporting organisations, are trying to use the energy of the youth to fuel political confrontation and spread anarchy instead of channelling it towards constructive work and nation-building," he said. "The youth of the country are being made pawns in the politics of anarchy," he stated. Singh alleged that the Congress and its allies want a change of government in India along the lines of Bangladesh. "They openly say at press conferences that they have drawn inspiration from Bangladesh for regime change, while another speaks openly about bringing down the government. This makes it clear that their only agenda is to dismantle democratic institutions and set the country on fire," he said referring to the uprising in Bangladesh in 2024 that toppled the Sheikh Hasina government. The defence minister said the use of terms such as "regime change" showed that the opposition's campaign was not about electoral reforms or issues related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. His remarks come amid massive protests in the national capital by opposition parties and civil society groups demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR process. Opposition leaders have alleged that the exercise lacks transparency and could exclude eligible voters. Referring to the Supreme Court's observations on Thursday, Singh said Gandhi and his allies need to understand that democracy does not permit attempts to create anarchy, undermine constitutional institutions or obstruct India's development. "Respecting the law is also essential to maintaining law and order. India's democratic institutions cannot be sacrificed at the altar of political self-interest," he said. Singh added that falsehoods, anger, attempts to malign institutions and political opportunism could not obstruct India's development. He advised Gandhi to respect the people's mandate and introspect on his political role instead of pursuing what he called "politics of destruction" in the name of protecting democracy. "India's future is everyone's responsibility. We must choose the path of dialogue and nation-building, not confrontation," Singh said.

stories.headline: RBI gives NoC to PFC-REC merger
stories.title: RBI gives NoC to PFC-REC merger
stories.summary: The merger of REC into PFC would create a financing entity with an aggregate loan book of over ₹11 lakh crore
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: State-run REC said on Friday that its has received a No Objection Certificate (NoC) from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for its proposed merger with PFC.
On June 28, 2026, the respective Boards of Directors of the Transferor Company (REC) and Transferee Company (PFC) approved the merger of the two power sector lending NBFCs.
“The company has received a No Objection Certificate from the RBI on October 15, 2026, subject to the instructions/ conditions specified therein,” REC said in a filing on BSE.

The scheme shall remain subject to such other statutory and regulatory approvals and fulfilment of such other conditions to the effectiveness of the scheme, including the approval of the respective shareholders and creditors of the companies involved in the scheme, as may be required in accordance with the applicable laws and the provisions of the scheme, it added.
The merger of REC into PFC shall create a financing entity with an aggregate loan book of over ₹11 lakh crore, it added.

The Share Exchange Ratio for the proposed merger of REC into PFC shall be 88 equity shares of PFC of ₹10 each fully paid-up for every 100 equity shares of REC of ₹10 each fully paid-up to be issued to the shareholders of REC as existing on a record date to be determined by the boards of PFC and REC (as may be applicable) at a future date, REC had informed on July 29 after the board approvals.
Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India is the Transaction and Tax Advisor and Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas is the Legal Advisor, to both PFC and REC.
Further, RBSA Valuation Advisors LLP was appointed by PFC and Ernst & Young Merchant Banking Services LLP was appointed by REC for providing joint valuation reports.
SBI Capital Markets was appointed by PFC and Nuvama Wealth Management was appointed by REC, to provide their respective fairness opinions on the joint valuation reports.

However, geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices and trade disruptions pose risks to the growth outlook, it added. "The question is whether these conditions will encourage private investment to play a larger role in boosting growth in the coming years. Recent indicators offer grounds for optimism. Gross fixed capital formation grew by 11.9 per cent in the first quarter of FY 2026-27, its fastest expansion in four years," Majumdar said. Deloitte Economic Outlook

stories.headline: CMRL-Exalogic case: Pinarayi Vijayan moves Supreme Court against Kerala HC order
stories.title: CMRL-Exalogic case: Pinarayi Vijayan moves Supreme Court against Kerala HC order
stories.summary: Former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan petitioned the Supreme Court challenging a High Court order directing an FIR against him, his daughter, and son-in-law over alleged illegal payments involving CMRL and Exalogic Solutions.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan has approached the Supreme Court challenging the Kerala High Court's direction to register an FIR against him in the CMRL-Exalogic case, based on information provided by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to the state police.

Senior advocate Siddharth Luthra mentioned the matter before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Friday, seeking an urgent hearing, citing the registration of an FIR and the possibility of coercive action against the CPM leader.
The Chief Justice said the matter could be listed on October 26 or 27, after the court reopens following the Dussehra break.
When Luthra pressed for an urgent hearing, the CJI said he could consider listing it before a special bench during the vacation, subject to the availability of judges.
Luthra argued that Vijayan, 82, faced the threat of being taken into custody following the registration of the FIR.

He also challenged the procedure adopted by the High Court, contending that a single judge had issued the direction in a writ petition resembling a public interest litigation despite not having the roster for PIL matters.
He further argued that the direction was issued without hearing the accused and that a division bench had refused to entertain their appeal.
Senior advocate N Hariharan also mentioned petitions filed by co-accused Veena T, Vijayan's daughter, and Mohammed Riyas, his son-in-law.
A single bench of the Kerala High Court had directed the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) to register an FIR under the Prevention of Corruption Act against Vijayan, Veena and Riyas.
The order came on a writ petition filed by K M Shajahan.
The High Court had rejected the state's decision to order a preliminary inquiry into the allegations.
It held that a preliminary inquiry was not warranted after the ED furnished information under Section 66(2) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).

stories.headline: India may raise fuel prices in November, says economist Alexandra Hermann Prasad
stories.title: India may raise fuel prices in November, says economist Alexandra Hermann Prasad
stories.summary: If authorities do not announce a fuel price increase in November, Oxford Economics’ inflation projections could decline by 10-30 basis points in the coming quarters.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'fuel price' in summary weight 24
article_sentences: The proposed increase could be around half the magnitude of the cumulative 7.5% hike implemented in May, the only period when retail fuel prices rose in response to the war in the Middle East.

Such an increase could push retail inflation to 6.2% in the October-December quarter and 6.5% in the first three months of 2027, both exceeding the Reserve Bank of India’s inflation target range of 2-6%, it said.
Oxford Economics’ projections are higher than the central bank’s estimates.
In its monetary policy review earlier this month, the RBI projected inflation at 6% for the October-December quarter, easing to 5.7% in January-March.
Oxford Economics expects price pressures to intensify next year, forecasting inflation at 5.4% for the financial year ending March, compared with the RBI’s projection of 5.2%.
If authorities do not announce a fuel price increase in November, Oxford Economics’ inflation projections could decline by 10-30 basis points in the coming quarters, the report added.

Inflation would nevertheless remain elevated, potentially prompting the RBI to raise interest rates by 25 basis points each at its December and February policy meetings, following a quarter-point increase in October.
Inflation rose to 5.54% in September, its highest level since late 2024, from 4.83% in August.

stories.title: CJP Tiranga Protest | 'If NDMC Order Is Disproportionate, We'll Act' : Supreme Court On Traders' Plea Against Delhi Central Park Shutdown
stories.summary: "If there is a loss of business, and we hold that it is unlawful to your clients, we will exercise our powers under constitutional tort jurisdiction," J Bagchi said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: "If there is a loss of business, and we hold that it is unlawful to your clients, we will exercise our powers under constitutional tort jurisdiction," J Bagchi said.

The Supreme Court on Friday orally observed that it will exercise its powers if there is any unlawful loss of business caused by the shutdown of Delhi's Connaught Place on account of the Tiranga protest announced by the Cockroach Janata Party.

On an oral mention seeking the listing of the petition, the bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi stated that if the restriction imposed by the New Delhi Municipal Corporation is found to be disproportionate, then the Court will act as per the principles evolved for compensation.
The Court agreed to list the matter on October 26/27, after the Dussehra break.

Advocate Jai Anant Dehadrai mentioned a petition filed by the Delhi Kirana Committee and Delhi Iron and Hardware Merchant Association expressing concerns over the call for protest made in the Central Park, which, he said, will obstruct trade worth Rs 200 crores a day.
He submitted that the New Delhi Municipal Corporation has put out a notice last night shutting down the place.
The bench then pointed out that the Delhi High Court was already hearing a similar matter.
The counsel however claimed that the present matter was different.
"It is not different.
They are all related.
Someone wants to protest, someone wants to sell moongfali, someone wants to law and order, all are related," Justice Bagchi said.
The counsel then submitted that since the festival season is coming, the obstruction of the place will cause huge loss of business.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks Sanjay Raut To Explain Remarks Against CJI & Judges While Entertaining INDIA Bloc Petition
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks Sanjay Raut To Explain Remarks Against CJI & Judges While Entertaining INDIA Bloc Petition
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (October 15) asked Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut to explain his remarks against the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and the judiciary while entertaining the petition filed by INDIA bloc leaders against the Election Commission of India (ECI).

In its order, the bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said that the petition was being provisionally entertained at Raut's instance, subject to him explaining his conduct.

Incidentally, Attorney General R Venkataramani granted consent yesterday to the Supreme Court Bar Association to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against Raut over his comments concerning the judiciary and CJI Surya Kant.

Raut had criticised the CJI for declining a meeting with Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, who had sought to meet the Chief Justice to raise concerns over alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Raut alleged that the CJI and several judges including the CJI had played badminton in London with BJP leaders and attended dinner parties with BJP ministers, but the CJI could not meet the Opposition leader.
During Thursday's hearing, the CJI had remarked that one of the petitioners would have to explain his conduct.
The CJI also observed that the judges were aware of statements being made outside the courtroom and were not living in "ivory towers".

While giving consent for criminal contempt proceedings, the Attorney General stated that Raut's statement on judges playing badminton with Ministers was false, and cited a Delhi High Court order which established this.
The AG also said that Raut's comments lowered the dignity of the judiciary and were scandalous in nature.
The petition was filed by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and 11 other INDIA bloc leaders challenging the Election Commission's actions in connection with the SIR of electoral rolls.

Apart from Congress leaders Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, Saugata Roy (Trinamool Congress-Mamata Banerjee), Akhilesh Yadav (Samajwadi Party), Tejashwi Prasad Yadav (RJD), Sanjay Raut (Shiv Sena UBT), MA Baby (CPI(M)), D Raja (CPI), Mahua Majhi (JMM), Supriya Sule (NCP Sharad Pawar) and ET Muhammed Basheer (IUML) are the other petitioners.
Two more opposition leaders, VCK President Thol.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks High Court to consider plea against Centre’s decision to take over Delhi Gymkhana Club
stories.title: Supreme Court asks High Court to consider plea against Centre’s decision to take over Delhi Gymkhana Club
stories.summary: The Court permitted 11 club members to move the Delhi High Court, after the High Court had earlier refused their plea on the ground that only the club could challenge the Centre’s decision
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (October 5, 2026) asked the Delhi High Court to consider a plea by 11 members of the Delhi Gymkhana Club, who had challenged the Centre's decision to take over the club's 27.3-acre premises and the subsequent eviction proceedings.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was told by senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the members, that the Delhi High Court had refused to entertain their plea on the ground that only the club could challenge the Centre's decision.
Mr. Singh said the High Court had asked the members to get a clarification from the Supreme Court that they could also move the plea there.
The Court permitted them to move the High Court, subject to objections that may be raised by the other side regarding maintainability and other legal oppositions.

Mr. Singh, appearing for the 11 members, had earlier told the Bench that a Central government-nominated committee was presently managing the club, and that it could not fight a legal battle with the government.

On September 3, 2026, the Centre, in a separate case, told the Delhi High Court that it would not take any coercive action until September 16, 2026, against the club in relation to its eviction from the premises on Safdarjung Road.

The High Court was hearing pleas by club member Vijay Khurana and others, seeking a stay on the June 29, 2026, show-cause notice for eviction issued to the club's management by an estate officer of the Land and Development Office (L&DO).

Vipin Aggarwal and ten other club members, in their petition filed through lawyer Nitin Saluja, sought the quashing of the resumption notification issued by the L&DO on May 22, 2026, and the show-cause notice issued by the estate officer on June 29, 2026.

stories.headline: Non-tariff barriers are biggest hurdle in India-China trade, says Nirmala Sitharaman
stories.title: Non-tariff barriers are biggest hurdle in India-China trade, says Nirmala Sitharaman
stories.summary: India-U.S. trade agreement would be concluded at the earliest, in the interest of global trade and bilateral economic ties between the two countries, says the Union Finance Minister
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Friday (October 16, 2026) expressed hope that the India-U.S. trade agreement would be concluded at the earliest, in the interest of global trade and bilateral economic ties between the two countries.
"I think recently the Indian Commerce Minister has also spoken that they expect and wish to have the agreement signed soon.
Negotiations have been going on.
I hope, in the interest of global trade and in the interest of trade between the two partners, India and U.S., the trade agreement gets concluded at the earliest," she said.
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday (October 15, 2026) said the first phase of the India-U.S. trade pact has been finalised and is undergoing legal drafting.

On trade with China, Ms. Sitharaman said the growing trade imbalance and persistent restrictions on market access for Indian products remained major concerns, despite years of engagement with Beijing.

India has consistently sought market access in China for products such as generic medicines, bovine meat, vegetables and other perishable goods, but made little progress despite years of engagement, Sitharaman said in an interaction with the Atlantic Council on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Thailand.

"Non-tariff barriers are the biggest hurdle in the trade between India and China," she said, adding that China had used phytosanitary measures and other non-tariff restrictions despite the potential for discussions and investigations to resolve such issues.

She said India had not adopted the approach of imposing punitive tariffs on trading partners to correct large trade imbalances, preferring instead to pursue negotiations, even if the process was time-consuming.
On BRICS, Ms. Sitharaman said the grouping should be viewed as a partnership aimed at improving the welfare of its people rather than as a platform to counter any country or bloc.
"I don't think BRICS's intention is to counter others.
It is more to strengthen the partnership through the BRICS," she added.
